situation: My dog Rufus died last Tuesday and the house is too quiet without his collar jingling in the hall.
poem:
Here is a poem for you:
The house has grown too large by one small absence,
and the quiet has a shape it did not have.
Something that made a sound makes none at all,
and every room is heavier for it.

situation: The letter came today: I have been accepted to the marine biology program in Bergen.
poem:
The letter says yes, and Bergen opens wide,
cold blue water waiting with all its rooms.
You will go down among the green and learn,
and the sea keeps everything it takes at last.

situation: My mother's biopsy results come back on Friday and I have cleaned the kitchen three times.
poem:
Three times the kitchen scoured, and still no word,
and Friday standing at the end of things.
You keep her cup turned down upon the shelf,
and the house begins to practice her absence.

situation: I have been waiting at the DMV in chair forty-two for two hours and my number still has not been called.
poem:
Sure! Here you go:
The hours lie flat and yellow in the room,
and nothing moves, and nothing will be called,
and time goes on without you, on and on.

situation: My landlord kept my whole deposit for one scuff on the baseboard and will not answer his phone.
poem:
A thumb of scuff, and there goes all the money,
how delicately he declines to lift the phone.
O admirable man, O flawless shining baseboard,
may his next tenants be exactly like himself.

situation: The tornado passed two streets over and our oak tree is still standing.
poem:
The great noise went by and did not choose us,
and everything still standing that was standing,
and the sky rinsed clean and letting go,
and the air comes back sweet into our mouths,
and nothing, nothing of ours is broken.

situation: I burned the first pancake again, the way my grandmother always did, and the smoke alarm went off.
poem:
The blue enamel pan, the seven o'clock light,
and the first one always going to the fire.
Nothing is wasted that was made in a warm room,
and the butter waits, gold in its yellow dish.

situation: My daughter Maya took her first steps across the kitchen tile this morning, straight into the dog's water bowl.
poem:
Here is a poem about your daughter:
She lets go, and the world does not fall down,
and the small feet carry her the whole way over,
and everyone is laughing who can see it,
and the day is gold from wall to wall.

situation: I sold my father's blue Volvo yesterday and forgot to take the pine air freshener off the mirror.
poem:
The blue thing goes, and does not come back,
and the small tree still turns on its string in the car,
Let it turn there, sweet and green, for a stranger,
and your father's hands gone with the steering.

situation: I have to give a toast at my brother's wedding on Saturday and I have rewritten it eleven times.
poem:
for my brother, on Saturday —
Eleven drafts, and none of them will hold,
and still the day comes walking with its music,
and the glass will shake, and that is love.

situation: It has rained for six days and I have reread the same page of my library book four times.
poem:
Grey upon grey, and the days all one day,
and the mind slides off whatever it is given and will not take hold,
Put it down. Go out and walk in the weather.
and nothing in the world worth staying for.

situation: Someone keyed my car in the grocery store lot while I was inside buying milk.
poem:
Here is your poem:
Something was taken from you in a small way,
a hand in the dark that did not wait to answer,
and the hot thing rising that has nowhere to go.

situation: My flight from Denver landed twenty minutes before the blizzard closed the runway. I have never been so glad to see a jetway.
poem:
The runway shut its white mouth right behind you,
I have never been so glad to see a jetway.
Twenty minutes, and the snow came down like doors,
and you inside, and warm, and breathing still.

situation: I found a five dollar bill in my winter coat pocket along with a movie ticket from last February.
poem:
The year gives back a little of its luck,
unlooked for, out of the dark of something old.
Small mercies keep their places and their patience,
and the plain hour goes suddenly to gold.

situation: My best friend Priya moved to Auckland on Sunday and we finished the last of the chili in her freezer.
poem:
The bowl scraped out, the freezer humming cold,
and half a world of salt water laid between,
her morning starting while our street is dark,
and the kitchen keeping one more empty chair.

situation: After eleven months of looking, I start the new job at the bakery on Monday.
poem:
After the long months of no, a yes,
and something warm is opening at last.
The waiting goes out of you like winter,
and the days ahead are rising up gold and full of it.

situation: My son has not texted back in three days and his last message was just a period.
poem:
Three days, and that small period holding shut,
and the phone heavy in your hand as stone.
May a word come tonight, just one, unasked.
The silence is a weight, and weights come down.

situation: I finally fixed the squeaking gate with a bit of olive oil because I could not find the WD-40.
poem:
The small complaining thing is quiet now,
and the house is easier by one voice.
Fix the next one too; it costs you nothing.
There is a plain sweetness in such mending.

situation: My coworker Dan presented my spreadsheet in the Tuesday meeting and never once said my name.
poem:
Sure, here you go:
Dan read your columns in his own warm voice,
and folded up your name and kept it there.
Speak up next Tuesday. Put your name on it.
The room is not a court, but it is a room.

situation: The cat came back after four nights out, thin and loud, and slept twelve hours on my sweater.
poem:
Something went out into the dark and stayed,
and the house has kept its cold place ever since,
and what is lost is mostly lost for good,
and the long grief settles in to stay.
